text:
Sam T: quick thread - prototyping a lightweight admit protocol for dedicated pools. goal: fast decision + safe accounting.
Lin Q: outline the minimal ops?
Sam T: admit(request_id, tenant, tokens, opts) -> provisional_id|deny. commit(provisional_id) or abort(provisional_id). also headroom(tenant, region) read + watch stream.
Javier M: provisional_id approach makes sense for races. what TTL are folks thinking? short - 15-45s range.
Priya K: 30s seems fine to start. needs operator tooling to reclaim leaked provisionals after TTL and surface them in admin UI.
Lin Q: admission should be idempotent. if client retries same request_id, admit should return same provisional_id or same denial. avoids double-reserve.
Sam T: agree. we'll mandate client-supplied request_id and server dedupe window >= provisional TTL.
Javier M: how to represent warmup cost? starting a new node or MIG is non-trivial. proposal: admit accepts warmup_hint: {type:"gpu_start", penalty_tokens: 5000}. runtime can choose fallback if it can't tolerate penalty.
Priya K: fallback choices: enqueue with ETA, downgrade to cheaper model, or run with reduced max_tokens. we should encode fallback_hint in deny response.
Lin Q: region-awareness: headroom(tenant, region) returns numeric headroom and provisioning_latency_ms. runtime then decides if cross-region migration is viable.
Sam T: good point. keep headroom simple: {headroom_tokens, burst_tokens, provisioning_ms}. but keep it as flat values in the API JSON response.
Javier M: we should also tag tenants with preempt_shield boolean. admit response must include preemptible: true|false so runtime sets QoS.
Priya K: observability: every admit/commit/abort must emit an event with request_id, provisional_id, tenant, outcome, reason, and region. add an admission_trace sample stream to correlate with SLO traces.
Lin Q: performance: admit must be <5ms p95 for hot path. for heavy checks (quota, billing), we can have async validators that may revoke provisional and force cancel if mismatch detected.
Sam T: revocation flow: soft-reserve can issue revoke(provisional_id, reason). runtime gets a stream event and should fallback/abort if revoke arrives before commit.
Javier M: testing: regression harness should simulate 10k concurrent admits with random drops and network flaps. assert sum(active_provisionals) <= committed + burst + safety_margin.
Priya K: we need admin endpoints: list_provisionals(tenant), force_release(provisional_id), simulate_headroom(tenant, region, delta).
Lin Q: billing: when do we bill tokens? on commit. but we should snapshot provisional charge to surface in billing UI as pending.
Sam T: rollout plan: alpha with a single dedicated shard + 2 non-critical tenants, collect metrics for provisional leak rate, admit latency, revoke frequency.
scale-bot: created issue INF-912: provisional-admit-metrics (TTL, leak-rate, latency).
Javier M: one more: burst lanes - I prefer integrated burst bookkeeping in soft-reserve rather than separate fast-path. allow a fast admit_burst(request_id, tokens) that gets special short-circuit checks but still yields provisional_id.
Priya K: agree. keep semantics consistent so audits don't get tricked by different codepaths.
Lin Q: handlers must be defensive: commit after long queue may fail if provisional expired. client should handle CommitFailed -> retry admit or accept fallback. document all error codes.
Sam T: action items: Lin write API proto + error code matrix; Javier build provisional store PoC; Priya design test harness; I'll draft admin UX for reclaim/visibility. reconvene in 10 days after alpha metrics.
Priya K: thanks all. :thumbsup:
